sources.title: Michael Wolf – Biography (photomichaelwolf.com)
sources.excerpt: michael wolf 1954 – 2019 lived in hong kong the focus of the german photographer michael wolf’s work is life in mega cities. many of his projects document the architecture and the vernacular culture of metropolises.

sources.title: Michael Wolf – Biography (photomichaelwolf.com)
sources.excerpt: wolf grew up in canada, europe and the united states, studying at uc berkeley and at the folkwang school with otto steinert in essen, germany. he moved to hong kong in 1994 where he worked for 8 years as contract photographer for stern magazine.

sources.title: Michael Wolf (photographer) – Wikipedia
sources.excerpt: His work takes place primarily in Hong Kong and Paris and focuses on architectural patterns and structures, as well as the documentation of human life and interaction in the city.

sources.title: Michael Wolf – Life in the City (Introduction, photomichaelwolf.com)
sources.excerpt: in his best known series on hong kong’s highly compressed, often brutal architecture, architecture of density, wolf uses the city’s sky-scraping tower blocks to great effect, eliminating the sky and horizon line to flatten each image and turn these façades into seemingly never-ending abstractions.

sources.title: Michael Wolf – Life in the City (Introduction, photomichaelwolf.com)
sources.excerpt: although hong kong is all but deserted in these images, minute signs of life creep to its surface… a shirt hanging out to dry or a silhouette behind a blind.

sources.title: Michael Wolf – Life in the City (Introduction, photomichaelwolf.com)
sources.excerpt: the formalism and deadpan approach of architecture of density echoes the work that emerged from the dusseldorf school of bernd and hilla becher. like the work of andreas gursky or thomas struth, wolf’s photographs reveal a desire to document and connect with the world around him, but with a contemporary visual approach.

sources.excerpt: The first book containing images from the series, Hong Kong: Front Door/ Back Door, was published in 2005.

sources.title: Herbert Ponting – Wikipedia

sources.title: Biography — Edward Burtynsky
sources.excerpt: Edward Burtynsky is regarded as one of the world's most accomplished contemporary photographers. His remarkable photographic depictions of global industrial landscapes represent over 40 years of his dedication to bearing witness to the impact of human industry on the planet.

sources.title: Biography — Edward Burtynsky
sources.excerpt: Burtynsky was born in 1955 of Ukrainian heritage in St. Catharines, Ontario.

sources.title: Biography — Edward Burtynsky
sources.excerpt: His imagery explores the collective impact we as a species are having on the surface of the planet — an inspection of the human systems we've imposed onto natural landscapes.

sources.title: Edward Burtynsky – Wikipedia
sources.excerpt: Most of Burtynsky's exhibited photography (pre-2007) was taken with a large format, field camera, on large 4×5-inch sheet film and developed into high-resolution, large-dimension prints of various sizes and editions ranging from 18 × 22 inches to 60 × 80 inches.

sources.title: Olaf Otto Becker
sources.excerpt: For more than 30 years now, landscape photography constitutes the main topic of my photographic work. I am especially interested in documenting the visible traces of human overpopulation left behind in nature.

sources.title: Olaf Otto Becker – Project: Above Zero
sources.excerpt: I show portraits of meltwater rivers that are increasingly appearing on the ice due to global warming. These were produced on two expeditions during which I traveled 450 km on foot in the melt zone of the Greenland Inland Ice with a companion.

sources.title: Olaf Otto Becker – Project: Above Zero
sources.excerpt: This series depicts how nature reacts causally to climate change and how these developments are confronted by humans.
